correctness.rationale: For the Hermitian equal-hop ring, loss-free sectors are precisely spectral eigenvectors annihilated by each positive-rate trap; finite-dimensional dissipative restriction decays off their reducing subspace. Bloch energy degeneracy occurs only for total flux 0 or π. At flux ell·π, partner k′=−k−ell; a trapped-node difference eigenvector exists iff q=n/g divides 2k+ell. Counting solutions and excluding selfpartners gives dim(0)=[g*gcd(q,2)−gcd(n,2)]/2, dim(π)=[g−1_{n odd}]/2 for q odd (else0). Summing squared overlaps of normalized partner differences gives at zero flux g*h/(2n) when gh∤2(r−a) and zero otherwise; at π flux the 0/g/(2n)/g/n three-level law by residue mod g. Other fluxes give zero. Independently diagonalized actual complex hopping matrices and computed absorber-kernel spectral projectors for EVERY 3≤n≤17 and all trap sets of size up to four, comparing all site probabilities at 0,π and generic flux; all agreed. This verifies finite cases only; universal algebra is the proof.
